scenes.visual: Title card: DOWNHILL, NOT RANDOM.

scenes.tts: Water picks the fold. But how does the chain find it, without trying every shape?
scenes.visual: A limp chain on screen; faint ghost copies of it flicker in many shapes. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: Water picks the fold. But how does the chain find it, without trying every shape?

scenes.tts: Count the options. Give each residue of a hundred-residue chain just three backbone shapes.
scenes.caption: Count the options. Give each residue of a 100-residue chain just three backbone shapes.
scenes.visual: A chain of 100 beads; above each bead, three small icons.
scenes.narration: Count the options. Give each residue of a 100-residue chain just three backbone shapes.

scenes.tts: One comes from each island of the map. Helix-like, strand-like, or left-handed.
scenes.visual: The three icons are labelled helix, strand, left-handed; a tiny Ramachandran map shows each icon coming from one island.
scenes.narration: One comes from each island of the map. Helix-like, strand-like, or left-handed.

scenes.tts: That gives a number of shapes with forty-seven zeros.
scenes.caption: That gives about 5 × 10⁴⁷ shapes.
scenes.visual: On-screen: 3¹⁰⁰ ≈ 5 × 10⁴⁷ shapes. No arithmetic is spoken.
scenes.narration: That gives about 5 × 10⁴⁷ shapes.

scenes.tts: Suppose the chain tried a new shape every tenth of a trillionth of a second. That is about as fast as a bond can turn.
scenes.caption: Suppose the chain tried a new shape every 10⁻¹³ seconds. That is about as fast as a bond can turn.
scenes.visual: On-screen: one shape every 10⁻¹³ s. A tiny bond icon spins.
scenes.narration: Suppose the chain tried a new shape every 10⁻¹³ seconds. That is about as fast as a bond can turn.

scenes.tts: Trying them all would take far longer than the universe has existed.
scenes.visual: A clock runs; a bar for the age of the universe (about 10¹⁰ years) is dwarfed by a bar for the search (about 10²⁷ years).
scenes.narration: Trying them all would take far longer than the universe has existed.

scenes.tts: Yet small proteins fold in microseconds to seconds. That gap is Levinthal's paradox.
scenes.visual: Label: real folding, microseconds to seconds. Title: Levinthal's paradox.
scenes.narration: Yet small proteins fold in microseconds to seconds. That gap is Levinthal's paradox.

scenes.tts: You know the Ramachandran plot forbids most backbone angles. Does that solve the paradox?
scenes.visual: A small Ramachandran plot appears beside the count. On-screen question: does the filter solve it?
scenes.narration: You know the Ramachandran plot forbids most backbone angles. Does that solve the paradox?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: No. The count already used it. Three shapes per residue is what the filter left behind.
scenes.visual: The three icons above each bead are shown coming out of the plot's islands. Label: filter already applied.
scenes.narration: No. The count already used it. Three shapes per residue is what the filter left behind.

scenes.tts: Now give each residue only two shapes. The search still takes billions of years.
scenes.visual: On-screen: 2¹⁰⁰ ≈ 10³⁰ shapes; billions of years.
scenes.narration: Now give each residue only two shapes. The search still takes billions of years.

scenes.tts: A filter on each residue makes each factor smaller. But there are still a hundred factors.
scenes.visual: A row of 100 boxes, each shrinking from 3 to 2. The row stays just as long.
scenes.narration: A filter on each residue makes each factor smaller. But there are still a hundred factors.

scenes.tts: So the answer is not fewer shapes. It is that the residues do not choose blindly.
scenes.visual: Text: not fewer shapes. Then: not blind choices.
scenes.narration: So the answer is not fewer shapes. It is that the residues do not choose blindly.

scenes.tts: Picture a flat golf course with one hole. Every wrong shape is as good as every other.
scenes.visual: A flat green plane with a single small hole.
scenes.narration: Picture a flat golf course with one hole. Every wrong shape is as good as every other.

scenes.tts: The ball rolls at random and almost never drops in. That is a random search.
scenes.visual: A ball wanders in random directions, missing the hole again and again.
scenes.narration: The ball rolls at random and almost never drops in. That is a random search.

scenes.tts: Now tilt the ground toward the hole from every side. Each roll tends to carry the ball downhill.
scenes.visual: The plane bends into a sloping bowl. Balls released from the rim roll toward the center.
scenes.narration: Now tilt the ground toward the hole from every side. Each roll tends to carry the ball downhill.

scenes.tts: This sloping landscape is the folding funnel. Its width stands for the many unfolded shapes.
scenes.visual: The bowl becomes a funnel. The wide rim is labelled many unfolded shapes.
scenes.narration: This sloping landscape is the folding funnel. Its width stands for the many unfolded shapes.

scenes.tts: Its depth stands for how favorable the contacts are. The native fold sits at the bottom.
scenes.visual: A vertical axis labelled energy (favorable contacts). The bottom is labelled native fold.
scenes.narration: Its depth stands for how favorable the contacts are. The native fold sits at the bottom.

scenes.tts: What makes the slope? The same forces that make the fold stable.
scenes.visual: On-screen question: what makes the slope?
scenes.narration: What makes the slope? The same forces that make the fold stable.

scenes.tts: Two oily side chains meet in the core. Some water is freed, and the energy drops a little.
scenes.visual: Two grey beads meet; a few water symbols fly off; the ball steps down.
scenes.narration: Two oily side chains meet in the core. Some water is freed, and the energy drops a little.

scenes.tts: A stretch of backbone makes its first helical hydrogen bonds. It drops a little more.
scenes.visual: A short helix forms with dashed lines; the ball steps down again.
scenes.narration: A stretch of backbone makes its first helical hydrogen bonds. It drops a little more.

scenes.tts: Partly correct shapes tend to last. Wrong contacts tend to break apart again.
scenes.visual: Green contacts stay; red contacts flicker and come apart.
scenes.narration: Partly correct shapes tend to last. Wrong contacts tend to break apart again.

scenes.tts: The chain needs only to keep more of what is right. A small preference at each step is enough.
scenes.visual: The ball descends step by step down the slope.
scenes.narration: The chain needs only to keep more of what is right. A small preference at each step is enough.

scenes.tts: For small proteins, the first few contacts climb a small hill. Once a core forms, the rest runs downhill.
scenes.visual: Near the rim, the ball climbs a small bump in the funnel wall. Label: first contacts. Past the bump, it rolls down the slope.
scenes.narration: For small proteins, the first few contacts climb a small hill. Once a core forms, the rest runs downhill.

scenes.tts: Real funnels have dips, called kinetic traps. Chaperones stop half-folded chains from clumping while they search.
scenes.visual: The funnel wall gets a rough dip; a ball stalls in it. A cage icon labelled chaperone surrounds a half-folded chain.
scenes.narration: Real funnels have dips, called kinetic traps. Chaperones stop half-folded chains from clumping while they search.

scenes.tts: Chaperones do not choose the destination. The sequence, in its environment, still does.
scenes.visual: The ball leaves the trap and reaches the bottom. Label: the sequence chooses.
scenes.narration: Chaperones do not choose the destination. The sequence, in its environment, still does.

scenes.tts: The rule bends in places. Disordered proteins have too few oily residues to pay for a core.
scenes.visual: A floppy chain that never collapses. Label: disordered region.
scenes.narration: The rule bends in places. Disordered proteins have too few oily residues to pay for a core.

scenes.tts: Prions take one sequence to a second fold, rich in beta sheet, that aggregates.
scenes.visual: One chain shown two ways: helix-rich (normal) and sheet-rich (prion), the second clumping.
scenes.narration: Prions take one sequence to a second fold, rich in beta sheet, that aggregates.

scenes.tts: And membrane proteins sit in lipid, not water, so their surface flips. Greasy residues face the lipid.
scenes.visual: A protein in a lipid band, greasy residues facing outward into the lipid.
scenes.narration: And membrane proteins sit in lipid, not water, so their surface flips. Greasy residues face the lipid.

scenes.tts: Folding is downhill, not random. Native-like contacts tilt the landscape toward the fold.
scenes.visual: End card. LINE: Folding is downhill, not random: native-like contacts tilt the landscape toward the fold.
scenes.narration: Folding is downhill, not random. Native-like contacts tilt the landscape toward the fold.
